newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate edges up from low prior close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate edges up from low prior close.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were up 55 basis points at 19.05 percent in early trade on Wednesday, in what traders said was a return towards average trading levels after an unrepresentative low prior close.
"Overnight rates may come under a little (upside) pressure. The market will remain stable, but rates could gain a little," a trader said.
Traders said early slippage by the peso against the dollar had also pushed secondary interest rates up.
Benchmark 48-hour contracts were meanwhile 0.75 of a centavo weaker at 7.8770/7.8785 per dollar.
Dealers said the peso had softened in the wake of a greater fall then was expected in primary interest rates.

Banco de Mexico assigned bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at 20.23 percent at Tuesday night's primary placement, a decrease of 238 basis points since last week. This compared with an average predicted fall of 139 basis points in a prior Reuters survey of money market traders.
Traders said a favorable outlook for inflation figures, due on Thursday, was helping to dampen upside pressure on secondary rates.
A Reuters survey of Mexico City financial houses MXAAP predicted an average rise of 0.64 percent for consumer prices during April 1-15.
Overnight rates on bank paper were down 60 basis points at 19.90 percent.
Liquidity of 3.487 billion pesos, and 600 milllion in bank bills, was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
